invariants: The declaration, not the chronology, is the coverage evidence: an empty-bodied approval (a good state) never hides a complete declaration on the same head, and a malformed declaration never falls back to an older one.
The newest review's state gates the evidence before any declaration is accepted: GOOD_STATES membership (APPROVED, COMMENTED) — a newest CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED review rejects coverage.
Every newest-review selection (latest_review verdict selector, declaring_review) breaks submitted_at ties by the later response position, mirroring the API's submission order.
A CHANGES_REQUESTED declaration is deliberately not coverage evidence even when followed by an empty approval on the same head (documented decision on PR #842's review).

The gate workflow's own poll (.github/workflows/coderabbit-gate.yml:269) STILL uses max() over its fetched list — the FIRST maximal element on a submitted_at tie — so a same-second APPROVED-then-CHANGES_REQUESTED pair on one head reads the APPROVED in the workflow's verdict while the verifier reads the blocking review: the two tie resolutions deliberately diverge (fail-closed verifier vs first-max poll). Measured as the workflow's own code; unifying the poll to the same (submitted_at, position) descending key requires editing coderabbit-gate.yml — a main-protected workflow file outside this PR's surgical scope, so the divergence is documented here instead of silently excluded (CodeRabbit round 14 on head 01096662). defect_knowledge_intake deduplicates by source ID, not by timestamp ordering, so no other family member carries the tie flaw.
